note: The pendulum of the BallJoint fixture with the same 3 m/s kick along z, now on a hinge about the z axis: the ball stays in the plane (z within 0.1 m) and `angle` (the turn of body 2 since load) is raised. The limits are minAngle -0.5 and maxAngle 0.5 rad: the bridge holds the ball against the limit (angle within 0.62, height above 3.9 m) while X_ITE, which ignores limits, swings far past them (its angle exceeds 0.7). In X_ITE the angle is the unsigned turn, in the bridge it is signed; the test reads its size.
gaps: minAngle, maxAngle, stopBounce and stopErrorCorrection are applied by the bridge (one-sided limit rows); X_ITE 16.6.0 makes a btHingeConstraint without limits, so it ignores them (see the limit fixture lines)
angle is signed in the bridge and unsigned in X_ITE (the angle of the axis-angle rotation)
angleRate comes from the angle change over the time since the last tick; X_ITE multiplies by the frame rate
